summary: Refactored build pipeline to use TargetRegistry, eliminating all hardcoded ternary branches on target literals from src/builders/.

Added resolveOutputDir() helper that builds a merged map from deprecated fields + outputDirs, supporting arbitrary custom targets without === equality checks.
Updated buildContext() to spread contextFlags from the registry definition instead of manually constructing the flag key string.
Updated buildPersona() and buildSuite() with optional registry parameter (defaults to defaultRegistry), wired through all call sites.
Updated resolveFrontmatterTemplate() to accept optional registry parameter; uses registry.get(target).defaultFrontmatter as fallback, replacing hardcoded ternary.

Updated build() to resolve registry from config.targetRegistry ?? defaultRegistry; uses registry.names() as default targets only when a custom registry is explicitly provided, preserving the historical ['vscode', 'claude-code'] default for backward compatibility.
Updated BuildConfig.targetRegistry JSDoc to remove the 'not yet consumed' note — the field is now fully wired.

comments.note: build() default-targets fallback uses the string literals 'vscode'/'claude-code' instead of registry.names() to preserve backward compatibility — because defaultRegistry now includes 'deep-agents' (registered by WP-001), using registry.names() would silently expand the default scope and break configs that don't declare a 'deep-agents' output dir. Consider adding a 'defaultEnabled' boolean to TargetDefinition so targets can opt-in/out of the default build set without requiring explicit targets[] config.

The two-registry pattern (defaultRegistry vs. a consumer-provided registry) means that calling buildPersona() or buildSuite() directly without passing a registry always uses defaultRegistry. If a consumer registers custom targets on a separate TargetRegistry instance and passes it only to build(), direct calls to buildPersona() will not see those custom targets. This is a minor API inconsistency that could cause confusion. Documenting this limitation in the JSDoc for buildPersona/buildSuite would help.

comments.note: src/targets/types.ts TargetDefinition.contextFlags JSDoc says 'Not yet consumed by the runtime… a follow-up WP will wire the registry lookup.' WP-003 already implemented this wiring in buildContext() in persona-builder.ts. The comment is now a direct factual contradiction. Must be updated before the documentation agent reviews this, or it will generate incorrect user-facing docs.

TargetDefinition.outputDirKey is declared as a required field in the public interface and used in registry.ts JSDoc examples, but is never read by the runtime. resolveOutputDir() uses the target name (first arg) directly as the key for the merged map — not outputDirKey. A consumer who registers name:'my-target', outputDirKey:'mydir' expecting outputDirs['mydir'] to be used will get a 'no output directory configured' error instead. Either the runtime should use outputDirKey for the map lookup, or outputDirKey should be removed/marked optional with a note that the runtime uses the target name.

No test in tests/builders/target-variable-injection.test.ts explicitly verifies target_deep_agents=true injection for the third built-in target. The code path is correct (shared with vscode/claude-code), but a dedicated test would protect against future regression.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied — src/targets/types.ts: replaced stale contextFlags JSDoc ('Not yet consumed by the runtime… A follow-up WP will wire the registry lookup') with accurate description reflecting that buildContext() already wires the registry lookup via registry.get(target).contextFlags. Fix-Forward applied — src/targets/built-in.ts: corrected module JSDoc from 'pre-populated with the two built-in targets' to 'three built-in targets: vscode, claude-code, and deep-agents'. WP-001/WP-003 added the deep-agents target but the comment was never updated.

BLOCKING: outputDirKey contract mismatch. TargetDefinition.outputDirKey is declared required and its JSDoc reads 'Key used to look up the output directory in the suite's output dir map.' However, resolveOutputDir() (persona-builder.ts ~L127) uses the `target` parameter (the name) directly as the map lookup key — outputDirKey is never read at runtime. For all three built-ins outputDirKey === name so no visible breakage. But any consumer who registers a custom target with outputDirKey !== name (e.g. name:'my-target', outputDirKey:'mydir') will receive a 'no output directory configured' error even when outputDirs['mydir'] is present. Fix: pass the TargetDefinition into resolveOutputDir() and use def.outputDirKey ?? target as the lookup key.

[documentation-forward] buildPersona() and buildSuite() in src/builders/persona-builder.ts accept an optional registry parameter defaulting to defaultRegistry. When a consumer passes a custom TargetRegistry only to build() and later calls buildPersona()/buildSuite() directly without the registry argument, their custom targets will not be visible. This two-registry limitation should be documented in the @param registry note for both functions.

[documentation-forward] BuildConfig.targets JSDoc in src/builders/types.ts reads 'Defaults to both vscode and claude-code when omitted.' This is no longer fully accurate: build() conditionally defaults to registry.names() when config.targetRegistry is explicitly supplied. Update the JSDoc to document the conditional default logic.
